text: ProtoGuy's 'Preview in Mirage' button really works and correctly recognizes he can face 16 directions, walk, and shoot -- but right now you steer him there with mouse clicks on an on-screen panel, not a gamepad. A real gamepad controller for ProtoGuy already exists, it's just only wired into his own separate demo scene, not into the Mirage preview.
details:
Good news: everything that makes ProtoGuy work -- his 16-direction aim, his composite torso+legs body, his gun -- is built purely through the Laubrary editors, no custom demoscene code. The 'Preview in Mirage' button in the Zoe editor does open a real preview window for him, and it correctly sees that he has earned all three abilities (turning, walking, shooting).

The catch: once that preview is open, the way you currently control him is a small on-screen box in the corner of the Game view with sliders and toggles you click with a mouse -- not a gamepad. A separate, already-working gamepad+keyboard controller for ProtoGuy does exist in the project, but today it only runs in his own dedicated test scene, not through the Mirage preview button.

Not yet double-checked: actually watching ProtoGuy's animation play correctly inside that Mirage preview window with a human's own eyes (this pass verified the button and the underlying logic fire correctly, and deliberately avoided force-closing an unsaved scene the user had open to do the full visual click-through). No physical gamepad was plugged into the dev machine to confirm button/stick presses at the hardware level either, in Mirage or in his own scene.

How to use this: open ProtoGuy's Zoe asset in the Zoe editor, scroll to the Rig section, and click 'Preview in Mirage' to see the button described above for yourself.
technicalDetails:
Live-verified this session (not just read) against the actually-open Laubrary Dev editor: reflection-invoked the private static ZoetropeWindows.PreviewInMirage(Zoe) (D:\UNITY\Laubrary Dev\Assets\Packages\Laubrary\Editor\Zoetrope\ZoetropeWindows.cs, ~line 1017) against the real ProtoGuy.asset (D:\UNITY\Laubrary Dev\Assets\Demos\ProtoGuyDemo\ProtoGuy.asset). A real Laubrary.Mirage.Editor.MirageWindow opened, confirmed via OS-level window enumeration (title exactly 'Laubrary.Mirage.Editor.MirageWindow'). Also live-derived ZoeCapabilities.Derive(ProtoGuy) -> aim=True(16 dirs) move=True fire=True(1) clips=5, confirming every manual-control affordance the HUD can offer is earned from real authored data.

Root of the gap: D:\UNITY\Laubrary Dev\Assets\Packages\Laubrary\Runtime\Mirage\MirageManualDriver.cs + MirageHud.cs's DrawManualControls() implement 'manual control' as a Play-mode OnGUI panel (Facing slider, Walk/Idle toggle, Move!=Facing toggle, Fire toggle) driven by mouse. Grepped all of Runtime/Mirage for Gamepad/IZoeInputSource/TopDownMotionDriver/NewInputSystemSource -- zero matches, no gamepad-reading code exists there. MirageManualDriver.Update() also PUBLISHES a MotionState override rather than moving the transform, so the character animates in place and never actually travels -- deliberate, to stay framed in the preview camera, but worth knowing if 'walk' is expected to traverse space.

The real gamepad+keyboard controller (Runtime/ZoeCharacter/TopDownMotionDriver.cs + NewInputSystemSource + ZoeCharacterControls.inputactions, built 2026-08-16 per project memory) is wired only into Assets/Demos/ProtoGuyDemo/ProtoGuySpawner.cs -> ProtoGuyDemo.unity, a separate path from Mirage. If gamepad-through-Mirage is wanted, the concrete next step is giving MirageManualDriver an optional path to read from IZoeInputSource/Gamepad.current instead of (or alongside) the HUD sliders -- a scoped addition, not a redesign.

During this session's live test, the open editor had an unsaved ProtoGuyDemo scene; PreviewInMirage's own EnsureMirageStageOpen() correctly prompted a native 'Scene(s) Have Been Modified' dialog before switching scenes. Deliberately clicked Cancel (not Save/Don't Save) rather than risk discarding whatever the user had open -- confirms the gate behaves safely, but means the MirageStage scene was never actually loaded this session, so the full visual composite-rendering-inside-Mirage check (as opposed to ProtoGuyDemo.unity, which IS extensively screenshot-verified per prior memory) is still outstanding. All scratch probe scripts (Assets/Editor/_T0087Probe.cs, _T0087Cleanup.cs) were deleted after use; git status on Assets/Editor/ confirmed clean.
